name: China Mobile Yangtze River Delta (Yangzhou) Computing Power Center / Data Center
notes: Phase 1 reported complete with one substation, two data hall buildings and one office building; overall project investment reported over RMB 10bn. Separate construction-service reporting describes planned B01-B06 data hall buildings and RMB 4.086bn estimated contract scope. No MW disclosed.

name: China Telecom Jiangbei Data Center / Jiangbei Computing Center (Yizheng Park)
notes: Opened in Yizheng in 2021; China Telecom invested project on 306 mu with reported total investment RMB 12bn. Later Jiangsu report says plan is 11 data buildings and 2 integration buildings, 32,000 high-power racks at full build, with 5 buildings completed and about 2,200 racks delivered as of 2024.

name: Tencent Yizheng Dongsheng Cloud Computing Data Center
notes: Opened December 2020. Reported footprint about 230,000 sq m / 350 mu and planned capacity for 300,000 servers; Jiangsu report says total investment over RMB 10bn, rooms 1-4 operational and full production expected in 2025. No MW disclosed.

name: Wangjie Big Data Center
developer: Jiangsu Wangjie Big Data Co., Ltd.
notes: Jiangsu SME public service profile places the company in Zhenjiang Economic and Technological Development Zone and says Wangjie is engaged in big-data-center/cloud infrastructure construction and operation, with an internationally planned green big data center providing 10,000 rack capacity and target PUE below 1.36. Zhenjiang's 14th Five-Year IT plan also identifies Wangjie as an ultra-large data center.

name: Yihualu Data Center / Zhenjiang data-center platform
notes: Zhenjiang's 14th Five-Year new-generation IT industry plan names Yihualu Data Center alongside Wangjie as an ultra-large data center supporting big-data analysis, applications, operation and maintenance. Source does not provide project address, phase, racks, or MW.

name: Zhuolang Technology Jiangxi Fuzhou Cloud Computing Big Data Center
developer: Zhuolang Technology / Jiangxi Zhuolang Data Center
notes: Large Fuzhou High-Tech Zone data center on Wang'anshi Avenue. Reported total building area 151,452 sq m, T3/Uptime Tier III and China A-level certifications, first phase operational and second phase near delivery in 2024; sources variously report 4,800 current racks, 4,092 planned in a case page, and up to 10,700 racks at full completion. No MW disclosed.

name: Sugon Cloud Computing Center, Fuzhou High-Tech Zone
notes: CRI/International Online reported Fuzhou was building four major data-center assets, including Zhongke Sugon Cloud Computing Center. China Daily partner content later described Fuzhou High-Tech Zone accelerating Zhongke Sugon cloud-computing technology park construction. No rack or MW figure found.

name: Chuangshiji High-Performance Computing / Supercomputing Center
notes: Identified in public reports as one of Fuzhou's 'two clouds, one supercomputing, one lake' data-center projects, with later reporting saying Fuzhou High-Tech Zone was advancing the high-performance computing technology park. No MW disclosed.

name: Yihualu Ganfu Data Lake
notes: Listed by CRI/International Online as one of Fuzhou's four major big-data-center projects. Treated as a data-lake/data-center infrastructure project; no phase, rack, or MW details found in accessible source.

name: Ganzhou Rongjiang New Area Cloud Computing Data Center Construction Project
developer: Ganzhou Rongjiang New Area Jinyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd.
notes: Rongjiang New Area public notice identifies the cloud-computing data-center construction project, owner and contractor, and says the project had passed initial completion acceptance by the five responsible construction parties. No MW or rack count disclosed.

name: Ganzhou municipal cloud-computing data-center estate (Tianyi Huawei Cloud, Mobile Inspur Cloud, Gannan Data Lake)
developer: China Telecom / Huawei, China Mobile / Inspur, Gannan Data Lake operators
notes: Ganzhou administrative approval bureau response states the city had three municipal cloud-computing data centers with 451 racks total: Tianyi Huawei Cloud 104, Mobile Inspur Cloud 105 and Gannan Data Lake 242, with total machine-room area 5,300 sq m. Treated as an operational estate because the source aggregates existing city-level centers.

name: Wan'an County Cloud Base
notes: Reported as Ji'an Telecom's first benchmark cloud-base project and Jiangxi's first county-level cloud project. Total investment about RMB 18m; cloud data center planned in two phases with 60 racks and 5,460 vCPU cloud resources, with phase 1 deploying 40 racks and 1,820 vCPU.

name: Ji'an municipal big data center / smart-city cloud computing center
notes: Xinhua reported Ji'an issued a plan to build a big data center relying on the municipal government information network and integrating existing cloud-computing platforms and government data resources. This appears to be civic cloud/data-center infrastructure; no capacity or later build status found.

name: Jingdezhen City Cloud Computing Center
developer: Jingdezhen municipal government / Inspur partnership / Envico contractor
notes: Envicool reported the Jingdezhen cloud computing center project was completed and supports centralized construction, operation and maintenance of city-level government IT systems. Earlier China Daily/PRN item says Inspur and Jingdezhen signed a cloud-computing/big-data strategic cooperation agreement. No MW disclosed.

name: China Mobile (Jingdezhen) Changnan Data Center
notes: Xinhua city report says Jingdezhen Mobile was actively building the China Mobile (Jingdezhen) Changnan Data Center, described as Jiangxi Mobile's only data center outside Nanchang and expected to meet Jingdezhen and surrounding cities' cloud-service demand for 20 years. No MW disclosed.

name: China Telecom Central China Cloud Computing Big Data Center / Poyang Lake Computing Center
notes: China Telecom and China Daily sources place the center in Jiujiang Poyang Lake Eco-Tech City, describe it as a Jiangxi 14th Five-Year/digital-economy key project supporting government, state-asset, medical, education, industrial and other clouds; China Telecom says the facility was rated a 2023 national green data center. No MW disclosed.

name: Jiujiang Central China Information-Technology Innovation Intelligent Computing Center
notes: Jiujiang News reported construction activity around an information-technology innovation project and said China Telecom would use the Central China Cloud Computing Big Data Center and the Central China Xinchuang Intelligent Computing Center as the core of a Jiujiang '2+3' computing-power system. No MW or rack count disclosed.

name: China Telecom Jiangxi Cloud and Big Data Center
notes: Jiangxi DRC approved the energy-saving report for the 2020 China Telecom (Jiangxi) cloud-computing big-data-center project at Nanchang Linkong Digital Economy Port. Later planning-permit notice covers A2 data center and A3 operations support center. Financial press reports total investment about RMB 2.1bn and 10,000 IDC racks at full build, but no MW disclosed.

name: China Unicom Zhi Cloud Data Center (Linkong)
notes: Located in China (Nanchang) Digital Economy Port; reported operational after about two years of preparation and construction. Built to international T3+ and national A-level standards, with 15,000 sq m building area, planned 3,000 racks and total planned investment RMB 2bn. No MW disclosed.

name: Jiangxi Artificial Intelligence Computing Center
developer: Nanchang / Jiangxi AI computing-center project company
notes: Xinhua Jiangxi reports project construction accelerating in Honggutan VR Science and Innovation City Phase II, west of Longhushan Avenue and north of Kechuang Street. Total investment about RMB 580m and planned in two phases. Source gives compute-center scope but no MW.

name: Huawei Jiangxi Cloud Data Center / Huawei Shangrao Cloud Computing Center
developer: Shangrao Big Data Industry Investment Development Co., Ltd. / Huawei Cloud
notes: Settled in Shangrao in 2017 and passed completion acceptance on 2019-11-14. Reported as Huawei's Jiangxi cloud data-center node, T3+ grade with 2,000 racks, 640,000 CPU cores, 1,024,000 GB compute resources and 100 PB storage/compute capability. National Data Administration case confirms Huawei Jiangxi Cloud Data Center was built in Shangrao.

name: Shangrao domestic Xinchuang AI Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Shangrao High-Speed Rail Economic Pilot Zone / Zhejiang University Computer Innovation Technology Research Institute partners
notes: National Data Administration case on Shangrao's citywide digital transformation says the city opened an international Internet data dedicated channel, built Huawei Jiangxi Cloud Data Center, and cooperated with Zhejiang University's Computer Innovation Technology Research Institute to build a domestic Xinchuang AI intelligent computing center. No MW or rack count disclosed.

name: Shangrao Xinrongyuan Big Data Smart Development Cloud Center
developer: Shangrao Xinrongyuan Big Data Technology Co., Ltd.
notes: Shangrao county/high-tech-zone project filing page describes a big-data smart-development cloud-center project intended to provide integrated hardware, software and data solutions and consolidate industry resources. No later construction status, rack count, or MW found.
